metaDescription: Seven propane gas grills compared on burner count, BTU per square inch, grate material, cooking area, side burner, warranty and assembly effort.
expertTake: The Char-Broil Performance Series 4-burner cabinet grill is our top pick for a proven brand, a 2-year warranty and the option to upgrade with a griddle or charcoal tray. The Char-Broil Classic 3-burner is the value pick for small households that want a straightforward grill. Skip gas if you want deep smoke flavour, because a gas grill is built for speed and control, and charcoal or a pellet grill does smoke better.
introParagraphs: A propane gas grill trades the ritual of charcoal for speed and control: turn a knob, wait about ten minutes for the grates to heat, then cook on a surface you can adjust in seconds. It suits weeknight burgers, chicken and vegetables where convenience matters more than smoke.

Headline BTU numbers dominate listings but say little by themselves, because a large number can come from an extra burner or a side burner. We evaluated seven models from the candidate pool using spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, and ranked them by how well the cooking area, burners and construction fit real use.

products.name: Char-Broil Performance Series 4-burner cabinet gas grill with side burner

specList.label: Extras
specList.value: 3 in 1: gas, griddle and charcoal upgrade

products.description:
The Performance Series is a four burner cabinet grill with a side burner, and the listing describes a 3 in 1 platform that starts as a gas grill and can be upgraded with a griddle or charcoal tray. That upgrade path is unusual at this tier and extends what one cart can do.

A two year limited warranty is a useful signal, because most grills in this price range offer a year or less. Against the Pro Series, the Performance has no infrared Amplifire cooking system and a shorter warranty, but it costs less. Against the Nexgrill four burner models, it offers a cabinet and the upgrade options rather than a higher BTU rating.

Plan on 60 to 90 minutes for assembly and a cover to protect the cabinet. Scrape the grates after each cook and empty the grease tray regularly. Owners who add the griddle mention that it turns the cart into a weekend breakfast station.
products.bestFor: Families who want a four burner grill with room to expand.
pros: Four burners and a side burner cover most cooking needs
Upgradeable with a griddle or charcoal tray
Two year limited warranty is better than many rivals
Cabinet stores the propane tank and tools
cons: No infrared searing system like the Pro Series
Upgrade accessories cost extra
Large cabinet footprint on a small patio

products.name: Char-Broil Pro Series Amplifire 4-burner cabinet gas grill with side burner

specList.label: Extras
specList.value: 3 in 1 with griddle and charcoal options

products.description:
The Pro Series uses the Amplifire infrared system, which puts a radiant surface between the flame and the food to even out heat and reduce flare ups. The listing also describes the same 3 in 1 upgrade options as the Performance Series and a three year limited warranty.

Infrared helps with consistent sear and with fewer hot spots, which matters for steaks. Against the Performance Series, the Pro adds the infrared system and a longer warranty at a higher tier. Against the Monument Mesa, which relies on a broil zone, the Pro is a different approach to the same goal.

Clean the infrared plates gently and keep the burners clear of grease. Replace the plates when they warp or crack. The warranty matters most here because the infrared plates are the part most likely to need attention.

Three year limited warranty is the longest here

products.name: Monument Grills Mesa 4-burner propane grill with Advanced Broil Zone, stainless

specList.label: Assembly
specList.value: As little as 30 minutes per listing

products.description:
The Mesa is a four burner stainless grill with 304 stainless steel burners and an Advanced Broil Zone that the listing says sears fast and adjusts for even heat. Assembly can take as little as 30 minutes, which is quick for a four burner cart.

The 304 stainless burners are more resistant to corrosion than lower grade steel, which is where many budget grills fail first. Against the Pro Series, the Mesa has no infrared system but offers a dedicated hot zone. Against the Nexgrill models, the Mesa focuses on the burner material and the broil feature rather than BTU.

Cover the grill in wet climates and burn off the grates after each cook. Check the burner ports for clogs once a season. Quick assembly is a real convenience if you are building it yourself on a weekend afternoon.
products.bestFor: Searing fans who want stainless burners and quick assembly.

products.name: Nexgrill 4-burner propane grill, 52,000 BTU, 562 sq in, cast iron grates, side burner
products.description:
The Nexgrill offers 562 sq in of cooking area and 52,000 BTU, with matte finish cast iron grates and a side burner. That area is enough for a large family cookout or a party of ten or more.

Cast iron grates hold heat well and give strong sear marks, but they need seasoning to avoid rust. Against the 60,000 BTU Nexgrill with 462 sq in, this model has more area and less raw output, which is a better ratio for even cooking. Against the Char-Broil Performance, it has a larger area but no upgrade options.

Oil the grates after each cook and cover the grill. Clean the grease tray monthly to prevent flare ups.
products.bestFor: Hosts who cook for a crowd and want cast iron grates.

products.name: Nexgrill 4-burner propane grill, 60,000 BTU, 462 sq in, warming rack, stainless body

specList.label: Cooking area
specList.value: 462 sq in total plus 164 sq in warming rack

products.description:
This Nexgrill lists 60,000 BTU across a total of 462 sq in of cooking space plus a 164 sq in warming rack, with a stainless frame and a side burner. The BTU figure is high for the area, which means strong potential heat but also a risk of uneven cooking if the burners are not well spaced.

BTU per square inch is a better measure than BTU alone, and this grill is at the high end of that ratio. The other Nexgrill has a larger area and lower output. The Monument Mesa has fewer BTU but a dedicated broil zone. If you want maximum heat for searing and a warming rack for rolls, this is the pick.

Cover the grill and clean the grates after each cook. Replace burner tubes when they corrode. Keep the burners clean, since high output grills are the least forgiving of grease buildup.

products.name: Char-Broil Classic 3-burner propane grill, 30,000 BTU, 360 sq in, porcelain grates
products.description:
The Classic is a compact three burner grill with 30,000 BTU, 360 sq in of primary cooking area and porcelain coated grates. The listing says it fits up to 12 burgers, which fits a family of four comfortably.

It skips the side burner and cabinet of the larger Char-Broil models, which is why it sits at a lower tier. Against the IdeaMaxx three burner, which is portable and has cast iron grates, the Classic is more conventional. Against the Performance Series, it gives up size and extras.

Porcelain grates are easier to clean but can chip, so avoid metal scrapers with sharp edges. Cover the grill and empty the grease tray regularly.

products.name: IdeaMaxx 3-burner propane grill, 38,200 BTU, cast iron grates, foldable side shelves
products.description:
The IdeaMaxx is a three burner portable grill with 38,200 BTU, cast iron grates and foldable side shelves. The cooking surface measures 302 sq in, about 23.6 inches across according to the listing.

The foldable shelves make it easy to transport and store, which suits tailgating and small balconies. The tradeoff is area, as 302 sq in is smaller than the Char-Broil Classic. For a household of two to four, it is plenty. Against the Char-Broil Classic, it offers cast iron and portability but less area.

Season the cast iron grates and keep them oiled. Fold the shelves carefully to avoid pinching.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cooking area is measured in square inches. The Char-Broil Classic offers 360 sq in, which fits about 12 burgers, while the Nexgrill 562 sq in model suits a crowd. The mistake is buying the biggest grill for a family of three and burning extra propane to heat it. The usual buyer mistake is paying for BTU and ignoring burner material.

Total BTU is misleading without the area. Dividing 52,000 BTU by 562 sq in gives about 93 BTU per square inch, while 30,000 divided by 360 gives about 83. Many experts treat 80 to 100 as a healthy range. A very high ratio, like the 60,000 BTU on 462 sq in, can lead to uneven cooking. Measure the primary area yourself, since listings sometimes bundle warming racks into the total.

Burners are the part that fails first. 304 stainless steel, as on the Monument Mesa, resists corrosion better than thin steel. Four burners allow zones for direct and indirect cooking, while three suffice for a compact grill. Use the BTU per square inch idea as a sanity check, not a rule.

Cast iron grates, like the Nexgrill 562 sq in and IdeaMaxx, hold heat and sear well but need seasoning. Porcelain coated grates on the Char-Broil Classic are easier to clean but can chip. Stainless steel grates are another option. Cast iron gains value if you plan to sear steaks and cook at high heat.

A side burner is useful for sauces and sides, but it adds to the BTU total without helping the main grates. The Performance Series adds a griddle option. Make sure you will use the extra before paying for it. A side burner can double as a way to keep sauces warm while you grill.

A longer warranty signals confidence. Char-Broil lists two years on the Performance and three on the Pro, while many others offer less. Assembly takes 30 minutes on the Mesa and longer on cabinet grills. Ask yourself whether the grill will live under a cover, because that changes how much stainless is worth.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cooking area and output
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared areas from 302 sq in on the IdeaMaxx to 562 sq in on the Nexgrill, and BTU per square inch. Models with a balanced ratio scored higher. Owner feedback patterns about rust and burner failure shaped our ranking more than BTU.

howWeEvaluated.title: Materials
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at 304 stainless burners on the Monument Mesa, cast iron and porcelain grates and cart steel. We did not run corrosion tests and rely on listings and owner feedback patterns. We compared listing claims of area and output against each other for consistency.

howWeEvaluated.title: Features and flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed the Char-Broil 3 in 1 upgrade options, side burners and warming racks. Useful features scored higher. We treated assembly time as a real part of ownership.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared warranty terms, three years on the Pro Series and two on the Performance. Longer terms scored higher. Warranty length counted as a signal of maker confidence.

howWeEvaluated.title: Assembly and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered assembly time, grease management and owner feedback patterns about burner life. Simple cleaning scored higher. Grease management features were weighed because flare ups are the main safety worry.

cards.text: A fast heat up, easy cleanup and a size that matches your usual meal. A side burner helps with sides.

maintenance.task: Burn off and brush the grates
maintenance.why: Residue carbonises and causes flare ups. A hot burn off and a brush keep grates clean.
Grease buildup is a fire risk. Replace the liner as needed.
Brush soapy water on joints to look for bubbles. Replace a cracked hose.
Spider webs and debris block flow and cause uneven flame. Use a thin wire.
Moisture rusts burners and cart steel. A cover extends life.

faq.a: No. Heat per square inch matters, and a very high figure can cause uneven cooking. The 52,000 BTU Nexgrill on 562 sq in is better balanced than a high figure on a small area. Many owners say a two zone setup is the single biggest improvement in everyday cooking.

faq.q: How many burners do I need?
faq.a: Three suit a small household, and four allow direct and indirect zones. Extra burners help most when cooking different foods at once. Match the number of burners to the number of foods you cook at once.
Cast iron sears better but needs seasoning. Porcelain is easier to clean but can chip. Season cast iron lightly with oil after each cook.

faq.q: How long does a gas grill last?
faq.a: Burners and cart steel are the usual limits, often several years with covers and cleaning. Stainless burners like on the Mesa last longer in damp climates. Covers and regular cleaning matter more than brand for long life.
It helps with even heat and fewer flare ups, particularly for steaks. The plates are a wear part and raise the price. If you cook steaks often, the infrared plate is worth considering.

faq.q: How do I check for gas leaks?
faq.a: Brush soapy water on the hose and joints with the gas on and watch for bubbles. Replace any part that bubbles and never use a flame to check. Always keep a fire extinguisher or a bucket of sand nearby when grilling.
